name: Hamipterus
isnote: Placed in its own family Hamipteridae within Pteranodontoidea/Anhangueria (Pêgas et al. 2019).
sum: Colonial crested pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Hami, Xinjiang, China, known from bonebeds with eggs and embryos.
holotype: IVPP V18931.1 — Shengjinkou Formation (Tugulu Group), Hami, Xinjiang (skull, probably female).
material: Remains of at least 40 animals in 3D, plus hundreds of eggs.
exceptional: Uncrushed eggs and embryos; crest horn sheaths preserved; one of the most important pterosaur nesting sites.
biology: Lived colonially by a lake. CT scans of embryos suggest hatchlings had well-developed legs but weak flight apparatus, and some parental care has been proposed.
author: Wang et al. 2014
